A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VITA study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–G support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v4 reports original robotic progress-estimation, expert-versus-scripted discrimination, Meta-World offline-RL, and ablation results.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The frozen CLIP encoder, adaptation module, regression head, meta-learning objectives, sequential inference updates, and dissimilarity-selection algorithm remain unchanged. Revised sampling hyperparameter documentation does not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same BridgeData V2 training coverage, ten expert evaluation datasets, five scripted datasets, and Meta-World MT10 tasks. No task, environment, or embodiment coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged in the corresponding experiments. Table 6's TTT-VIS label becomes TTT-RS, matching the memoryless variant already described in v4; this is not a replacement baseline.

E3.justification: Appendix D.1 changes the reported sampling defaults from stride 2 and 16 windows to stride 1 and 8 windows, matching Section 4.1. Appendix F.1 replaces the dissimilarity-ablation stride floor(w_tr/2) with the common stride s. These are revisions to stated settings; the PDFs do not establish experimental reruns.

E4.justification: Appendix F.1 revises the documented sampling-ablation setup by replacing its window-dependent candidate stride with the common stride s. The discrimination question, compared sampling variants, and Table 5 outcomes remain unchanged. No additional robustness or supplementary analysis is introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report ten random seeds for offline RL, IQM returns, and 95% confidence intervals using 10,000 bootstrap resamples stratified by task. No uncertainty-reporting practice or repeated-run information changes.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and discrimination checkmarks in Tables 1–6 are retained, with no added or removed result rows. For example, Table 2 retains VITA's IQM of 0.815 and META-WL's 0.779. The reported qualitative findings also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The value-function definitions, Equations 1–5, and Appendix G's complexity derivation remain unchanged. Replacing r with w_tr for the existing eight-frame window is a notation correction.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and concluding discussion retain the same central claims about test-time adaptation, generalization, temporal reasoning, and zero-shot reward shaping. No new core contribution or stronger performance claim appears.

C2.justification: Section 5.1 refines the suggested applicability from any vision-language representation-learning method to pretrained representations encoding a universal value function. Section 6.2 adds an explicit discussion of possible extensions to domain-specific representations through encoder-agnostic adaptation. Existing experimental interpretations and limitations remain.

D1.justification: v5 adds a project-website link and corrects the appendix sampling defaults to agree with the main training setup. Architecture, optimizer, hardware, and offline-RL implementation disclosures otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The introduction replaces the Octo citation with OpenVLA, adds SIMA, and removes Navigation World Models. Section 2.2 adds an explicit LSTM reference where v4 had an unresolved citation. These are limited citation changes; the principal positioning against prior value estimators remains.

P1.justification: v5 adopts author-year citations and an alphabetical bibliography, updates author information and acknowledgments, standardizes GVL and TTT-RS names, and removes repeated explanation in Appendix F.2. Most prose and the section hierarchy remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is reformatted with separate subcaptions and 'Value Function Head' labels replacing 'MLP.' Figure 3 and Tables 1 and 6 move with text reflow; table captions and the TTT-RS header receive limited corrections. Conference headers are added, while the remaining visual content is retained.

improvement.justification: v5 improves reproducibility and readability by resolving conflicting sampling settings across Section 4.1 and the appendices and correcting Table 6's memoryless-variant label. The project link and modest presentation refinements provide additional benefits. These are limited improvements to an otherwise unchanged scientific contribution and empirical record.
